- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.15), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if price is rising.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward spikes in sentiment; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 1.5σ above recent 7-day average, reduce by 10–15%.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags true trend by 2–3 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is trending.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes, model underreacts; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to compensate.
- When sentiment is flat (±0.05), model tends to drift; anchor forecast to 14-day moving average.
